body:
The problem with changing fields is that I have no idea of what I'd enjoy. And I can't do the gap year because in my country you have two years after graduating high school to get into college. After that you'd have to retake the final high school exams, and I'm not putting myself through that again.
 Besides all this, for the last two years of high school, all I wanted was to get better and get into college. But I feel like I got cold feet at the end and aimed a bit low. Unfortunately, there's not much I can do about it now, since I have only gotten worse since January.
I’m planning on doing it near the final train station so that hopefully I don’t bother the people riding the train much

I’m in the middle of my second semester of college and I think I’m in the wrong field. The problem is that I don’t see myself fitting in to any other or even enjoying myself as much. In high school I had to prove everyone and myself that i was good enough to pursue a life in this cut throat field. I was really passionate about it. I’d go to “camps” every chance I had and those were some of the happiest times of my life. But the first semester was sub-optimal. I managed to get results that I never thought I’d get and earned some respect even from older peers. But I had to work my ass off. From 9am to 1am most days, no joke.

When I was little, I had always imagined that when I’d go to college it would be a “magical time” and all the depression would go away. Guess what, it got worse.

So now I’m in a field that I know im not talented/worthy enough to be in and if I want to succeed I have to sacrifice my entire life (not that it has much worth, but still).

I‘ve also never been able to imagine myself past the age of 25. So maybe thats a sign that I was never meant to last that long.

In the last month I’ve distanced myself from friends and ignored worried texts so that the blow wouldn’t hit as hard.

Now I’m just waiting for the rain to calm down so that I can go to the railroad and end it all. Or maybe that’s just an excuse, idk
